what_it_does: This paper presents 3D-SubG, a chip designed to accelerate a class of graph neural networks (GNNs) — AI models that operate on graph-structured data such as social networks or molecular structures. The specific variant, subgraph GNNs, works by breaking the full graph into many small overlapping subgraphs and processing each independently, which is more expressive but creates irregular, hard-to-predict memory access patterns that swamp the bandwidth of conventional chips. 3D-SubG physically stacks a logic die (the computation layer) directly on top of a DRAM die (the main memory layer) using a technique called hybrid bonding, which creates extremely short, dense electrical connections between them, dramatically cutting the energy and time cost of moving data. On the logic die, SRAM-based processing-in-memory macros (blocks of fast on-chip memory that can also multiply numbers) carry out computation close to where data is stored. An additional technique identifies and skips zero values in the sparse graph adjacency structure — since most pairs of nodes in a large graph are not connected, many entries are zero and can be ignored, reducing wasted work.
